title: How many traits a person should start with, and how the count should vary
question: When a person is generated, how many temperament traits should they carry at the start — a fixed number, a range, or a distribution that varies by age and by how much of their life the game has already recorded? And should the player's own starting count differ from an NPC's?
whyItMatters: The trait pack seam is built, so generation is about to start writing traits onto every generated person and the count is a parameter that has to be chosen now. Too many and everyone reads as a caricature and the person card becomes a list; too few and personality never reaches conversation or decisions often enough to be felt. lamontae gave a starting answer of one or two on 2026-09-22 and said in the same breath that it will be adjusted, so the number is provisional and the shape behind it — whether it is flat, age-weighted, or grows as a life accumulates recorded history — has not been decided at all.
usableAnswer: A recommended starting count or distribution, stated as something generation can implement directly (for example: one trait at generation, a second added at a named life stage, at most N ever held); whether it varies with age or recorded history; whether the player differs from an NPC; and the reasoning, with reference to how comparable simulation games handle trait counts at character creation and over a lifetime.

sourcesChecked.source: lamontae's own messages, 2026-09-22 03:36 and 04:11 (owner record 01, section A)
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Gives 'one or two' as a starting answer and says explicitly that it will be adjusted. Settles that the number is small; settles nothing about how it varies, how it grows, or whether the player differs.
Specifies what a trait is, how a pack declares movability and how resistance is read from the record chain. It does not specify how many traits a generated person starts holding.
Measures what the game has against what the transcripts proposed. It identified the count as an open question rather than answering it.

notes: Filed under the rule lamontae set on 2026-09-22: a judgment about how the simulated world should feel goes to ChatGPT as a brief, and ChatGPT comes back to him. It is not a question to put to him directly again.
His starting answer of one or two is the working default until this is answered; generation should not block on it.

answer.summary:
Keep the owner's one-or-two salient starting descriptors as the working adult baseline. For the first private comparison use a 50/50 one-versus-two draw; this is explicitly authored calibration, not a measured human distribution or an owner-selected exact percentage. It applies to salient descriptors, not deletion/zeroing of the five underlying dimensions. Existing meaningful generated traits are not discarded to satisfy a display budget.

Use the same underlying generation policy for NPCs and the player. The player can confirm/change/skip their suggested profile; observers see only justified impressions about others. Age informs plausible experiences and the evidence behind a disposition, not a fixed birthday that awards another trait. No automatic lifelong maximum, no count that rises every time another memory is written. Adding later nuance can mean clearer recognition of existing character as well as actual development. Strong adult moral/role labels should not be assigned to young children simply to fill two slots.

Acceptance ChatGPT requests (not executed): Generate adults with one/two salient descriptors while other represented dimensions remain available; verify same seed and version repeat. No automatic extra trait after a birthday or ten events. Observer card does not show unknown latent descriptors.
